## 1. The editor

CCN String Diagrams is a box-and-arrow editor for the graphical calculus of monoidal categories. It runs in one HTML page, online or offline. The canvas on the left holds the diagram; the panel on the right holds the expression, a keypad of the book's symbols, the three main buttons and the result.

![The editor with Figure 2.3 loaded and simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

- **Expression → Diagram** draws the typed expression.
- **Diagram → Expression** reads the drawn diagram back as an expression, in the book's notation.
- **Simplify** rewrites the diagram step by step with the rules of the book, shows every step with the name of the rule used, and, for an equation, says whether both sides reach the same normal form.

Every example in this document is in the editor's **Load an example…** menu. Loading one fills in the expression and the signature, sets the duals mode, and draws the diagram. Each section below shows the expression (symbolic), the diagram the editor draws (graphical), and what Simplify does with it. The pictures are screenshots of the editor itself.

## 2. Conventions and typing

The editor follows the book:

- **Diagrams read bottom to top.** Sources are at the bottom and targets at the top, so in $gf$ the box $f$ sits below $g$. (The direction can be flipped in the toolbar.)
- **Composition is juxtaposition:** `g f` is $gf$. It binds tighter than $\otimes$; `g ∘ f` and `f ; g` are also accepted.
- **$\otimes$ is side by side**, left to right. Type `⊗` (or `(x)`).
- **The unit** $\mathbb 1$ is typed `𝟙`, `I` or `1`, and is never drawn.
- **Identities** are `id_X`; tensor colours are written in braces, `id_{X⊗Y}` or `ev_{Y⊗X}`.
- **Duals.** With *duals: ∨X* (§2.1.2) the left dual is `∨X`, and `ev_X`, `coev_X`, `∨f` are built in. With *duals: X\** (§2.1.3, pivotal) the dual is `X*`, arcs carry arrows ($X$ points down, $X^*$ points up), and `ev_X`, `ev~_X` ($\widetilde{\mathrm{ev}}_X$), `coev_X`, `coev~_X` ($\widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_X$) and `f*` are built in.

The **signature** box declares the boxes, one per line:

```
f : X → Y
g : Y → Z
ω : X ⊗ Y → 𝟙
Ω : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
pairing ω Ω
```

`pairing ω Ω` says that $\Omega$ is the inverse of the pairing $\omega$, so the zigzag rules may cancel them. The keypad (tabs *Book*, *Greek*, *Letters*) types every symbol, and the preview under the expression typesets it as in the book.

## 3. How the simplifier works

The simplifier works on the **layered form** of a diagram: the source colours, then one box per layer, each with the number of arcs to its left. **Level exchange** (Figure 2.1) lets two layers swap when their boxes do not touch, and every diagram is brought to a normal form in which boxes sit as low and as far left as they can. The rules are then tried in this order, and the first one that applies is used:

| Rule | Book | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| unit strands, ⊗-coloured strands | §2.1.2 | erase arcs coloured $\mathbb 1$; split an arc coloured $X\otimes Y$ into two |
| caps and cups on ⊗ (pivotal) | §2.2 | $\mathrm{ev}_{Y\otimes X}=\mathrm{ev}_X(\mathrm{id}_{X^*}\otimes\mathrm{ev}_Y\otimes\mathrm{id}_X)$ and the same for coev, ẽv, c̃oev |
| (2.1) left zigzag, (2.1) right zigzag | (2.1), Fig. 2.2 | cancel a pairing and its inverse that form a zigzag |
| definition of ∨f / Fig. 2.3 fold (left) | §2.1.2, Fig. 2.3 | fold cup–box–cap into the dual box |
| Fig. 2.3 fold (right) | Fig. 2.3 | the same with ẽv and c̃oev |
| (2.2) slide through ev / coev, Fig. 2.4 slides | (2.2), Fig. 2.4 | move a dual box across a cap or cup |
| Lemma 2.3 (X\*\* = X), ψ = id (X\*\* = X) | §2.3.1 | with $X^{**}=X$: $\mathrm{ev}_{X^*}=\widetilde{\mathrm{ev}}_X$, $\mathrm{coev}_{X^*}=\widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_X$ and the reverse, and $\psi_X=\mathrm{id}_X$ |
| trace symmetry (§2.6.1) | §2.6.1 | turn a loop so that its boxes start at the first name in code-point order |
| inverse boxes | §2.6.2 | cancel $u'u$ and $uu'$ for a declared pair `inverse u u′` |
| sphericity (§2.7.1) | §2.7.1 | spherical only: a right loop becomes a left loop |
| retract (§2.7.3) | §2.7.3 | cancel $pj$ for a declared retraction `retract p j` |
| braiding on ⊗ (3.1)–(3.3) | §3.1.1 | split a crossing of tensor products into crossings of single strands; remove a crossing with $\mathbb 1$ |
| R2 (§3.2.2) | §3.2.2 | a crossing and its inverse cancel |
| R4, R5: naturality of τ | §3.1.1, §3.2.2 | a one-line box moves from above a crossing to below it |
| R3: Yang–Baxter | Exercise 3.1.12 | three crossings of one kind on positions $a, a+1, a$ become $a+1, a, a+1$ |
| twist fold (§3.3.1) | §3.3.1, Lemma 3.2 | pivotal only, tried before Lemma 2.3: a curl (cup, crossing, cap) becomes $\theta^l_X$, $\theta^r_X$ or an inverse; layers that do not touch the curl may sit between its parts |
| twists cancel, naturality of θ | Lemma 3.2 | a twist and its inverse cancel; a twist moves below a one-line box |
| twist on ⊗ (Exercise 3.3.3) | Exercise 3.3.3 | $\theta_{X\otimes Y} = (\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\tau_{Y,X}\tau_{X,Y}$, $\theta_{\mathbb 1} = \mathrm{id}$ |
| ribbon: θʳ = θˡ (§3.3.2) | §3.3.2, Cor. 3.4 | ribbon only: the right twist is the left twist; ribbon also switches on sphericity |
| symmetry (§3.1.2), τ_Y,X τ_X,Y = id | §3.1.2 | symmetric only: under-crossings become over-crossings, and a crossing twice is the identity |

Each step is shown with its rule name. An equation holds when all its sides reach the same normal form. Every rule makes the diagram smaller, so Simplify always stops.

## 4. §2.1.1–2.1.2 Categories and monoidal categories

### §2.1.1  id_X

§2.1.1 draws the identity of an object $X$ as a plain vertical arc coloured $X$, with no box. Every arc in the editor is an identity.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → Y
g : Y → Z
```

```
id_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\mathrm{id}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§2.1.1  id_X](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** Type `id_X`. The two dots are the free ends: the source $X$ at the bottom and the target $X$ at the top.

No rewriting rule applies: the diagram is already in normal form.

### §2.1.1  f : X → Y

A morphism $f\colon X\to Y$ is a box with its source arc coming in from below and its target arc leaving at the top.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → Y
g : Y → Z
```

```
f
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
f
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $Y$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§2.1.1  f : X → Y](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The signature line `f : X → Y` declares the box; the expression `f` then draws it. Diagram → Expression reads it back as $f$.

No rewriting rule applies: the diagram is already in normal form.

### §2.1.1  composition gf

The composition $gf$ is drawn by stacking: $f$ below $g$, joined by the arc $Y$. The book writes composition by juxtaposition, and so does the editor.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → Y
g : Y → Z
```

```
g f
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
g f
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $Z$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§2.1.1  composition gf](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** Type `g f`. Juxtaposition binds tighter than $\otimes$, so `g f ⊗ h` means $(gf)\otimes h$. `g ∘ f` and `f ; g` are accepted too.

No rewriting rule applies: the diagram is already in normal form.

### §2.1.2  f ⊗ g

§2.1.2: the monoidal product $f\otimes g$ is drawn by placing the boxes side by side, $f$ on the left.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → Y
g : U → V
```

```
f ⊗ g
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
f \otimes g
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes U$ to $Y \otimes V$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§2.1.2  f ⊗ g](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** `f ⊗ g` with `f : X → Y` and `g : U → V`. The source $X\otimes U$ is read left to right along the bottom.

No rewriting rule applies: the diagram is already in normal form.

### §2.1.2  f : X ⊗ Y → A ⊗ B ⊗ C

A box may have several arcs on each side; their colours are read left to right.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X ⊗ Y → A ⊗ B ⊗ C
```

```
f
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
f
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes Y$ to $A \otimes B \otimes C$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§2.1.2  f : X ⊗ Y → A ⊗ B ⊗ C](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** `f : X ⊗ Y → A ⊗ B ⊗ C` gives a box with two inputs and three outputs.

No rewriting rule applies: the diagram is already in normal form.

### §2.1.2  boxes with source or target 𝟙: α, β, γ

The unit object $\mathbb 1$ is never drawn. A morphism $\mathbb 1\to\mathbb 1$ is a box with no arcs, $\mathbb 1\to X$ has no arc below, and $X\to\mathbb 1$ has none above.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
α : 𝟙 → 𝟙
β : 𝟙 → X
γ : X → 𝟙
```

```
α ⊗ β ⊗ γ
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\alpha \otimes \beta \otimes \gamma
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§2.1.2  boxes with source or target 𝟙: α, β, γ](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** Type the unit as `𝟙` (also `I` or `1`). Simplify erases strands coloured $\mathbb 1$.

No rewriting rule applies: the diagram is already in normal form.

### Figure 2.1  level-exchange property

Figure 2.1, the level-exchange property: boxes on different arcs can slide past each other, so $f\otimes g = (\mathrm{id}_Y\otimes g)(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_U) = (f\otimes \mathrm{id}_V)(\mathrm{id}_X\otimes g)$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → Y
g : U → V
```

```
f ⊗ g = (id_Y ⊗ g)(f ⊗ id_U) = (f ⊗ id_V)(id_X ⊗ g)
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
f \otimes g
$$

$$=$$

$$
(\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes g) (f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{U})
$$

$$=$$

$$
(f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{V}) (\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes g)
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes U$ to $Y \otimes V$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![Figure 2.1  level-exchange property](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** Simplify puts each side in its level-exchange normal form (one box per layer, boxes pushed down and to the left). All three sides reach the same normal form, so the verdict says the equation holds, without any other rule.

No rewriting rule applies: the diagram is already in normal form, and all sides have the same normal form.

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

## 5. §2.1.2 Pairings and the zigzag identities (2.1)

### (2.1) left: (id_Y ⊗ ω)(Ω ⊗ id_Y) = id_Y

Formula (2.1), left: for a non-degenerate pairing $\omega\colon X\otimes Y\to\mathbb 1$ with inverse $\Omega\colon\mathbb 1\to Y\otimes X$, the zigzag on $Y$ straightens: $(\mathrm{id}_Y\otimes\omega)(\Omega\otimes\mathrm{id}_Y)=\mathrm{id}_Y$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
ω : X ⊗ Y → 𝟙
Ω : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
Ω′ : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
pairing ω Ω
pairing ω Ω′
α : T → Z ⊗ X
β : T ⊗ Y → Z
```

```
(id_Y ⊗ ω)(Ω ⊗ id_Y) = id_Y
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
(\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes \omega) (\Omega \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y}) \;=\; \mathrm{id}_{Y}
$$

a morphism from $Y$ to $Y$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![(2.1) left: (id_Y ⊗ ω)(Ω ⊗ id_Y) = id_Y](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The signature line `pairing ω Ω` tells the simplifier that $\omega$ and $\Omega$ are paired. The rule **(2.1) left zigzag** removes the cup $\Omega$ and the cap $\omega$ together.

Steps, side by side: side 1: (2.1) left zigzag; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{id}_{Y}
$$

![(2.1) left: (id_Y ⊗ ω)(Ω ⊗ id_Y) = id_Y, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### (2.1) right: (ω ⊗ id_X)(id_X ⊗ Ω) = id_X

Formula (2.1), right: $(\omega\otimes\mathrm{id}_X)(\mathrm{id}_X\otimes\Omega)=\mathrm{id}_X$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
ω : X ⊗ Y → 𝟙
Ω : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
Ω′ : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
pairing ω Ω
pairing ω Ω′
α : T → Z ⊗ X
β : T ⊗ Y → Z
```

```
(ω ⊗ id_X)(id_X ⊗ Ω) = id_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
(\omega \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X}) (\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \Omega) \;=\; \mathrm{id}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![(2.1) right: (ω ⊗ id_X)(id_X ⊗ Ω) = id_X](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The rule **(2.1) right zigzag** straightens the zigzag on $X$.

Steps, side by side: side 1: (2.1) right zigzag; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{id}_{X}
$$

![(2.1) right: (ω ⊗ id_X)(id_X ⊗ Ω) = id_X, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### Uniqueness of the inverse (try “right zigzag first”)

The inverse of a pairing is unique. If $\Omega$ and $\Omega'$ are both inverses of $\omega$, the diagram $(\mathrm{id}_Y\otimes\omega\otimes\mathrm{id}_X)(\Omega'\otimes\Omega)$ equals $\Omega$ by one zigzag and $\Omega'$ by the other.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
ω : X ⊗ Y → 𝟙
Ω : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
Ω′ : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
pairing ω Ω
pairing ω Ω′
α : T → Z ⊗ X
β : T ⊗ Y → Z
```

```
(id_Y ⊗ ω ⊗ id_X)(Ω′ ⊗ Ω)
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
(\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes \omega \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X}) (\Omega ' \otimes \Omega)
$$

a morphism from $\mathbb{1}$ to $Y \otimes X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![Uniqueness of the inverse (try “right zigzag first”)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** With the default order the left zigzag fires first and the result is $\Omega$. Tick **right zigzag first** and Simplify gives $\Omega'$ instead: the two answers together prove $\Omega=\Omega'$.

Steps: (2.1) left zigzag.

Normal form:

$$
\Omega
$$

![Uniqueness of the inverse (try “right zigzag first”), simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

### (1.10)  backward ∘ forward = id

The bijection (1.10) $\mathrm{Hom}(T, Z\otimes X)\cong\mathrm{Hom}(T\otimes Y, Z)$ sends $\alpha$ to $(\mathrm{id}_Z\otimes\omega)(\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_Y)$; the way back sends $\beta$ to $(\beta\otimes\mathrm{id}_X)(\mathrm{id}_T\otimes\Omega)$. Going there and back gives $\alpha$ again.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
ω : X ⊗ Y → 𝟙
Ω : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
Ω′ : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
pairing ω Ω
pairing ω Ω′
α : T → Z ⊗ X
β : T ⊗ Y → Z
```

```
((id_Z ⊗ ω)(α ⊗ id_Y) ⊗ id_X)(id_T ⊗ Ω) = α
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(((\mathrm{id}_{Z} \otimes \omega) (\alpha \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y})) \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{T} \otimes \Omega)
\end{aligned}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\alpha
$$

a morphism from $T$ to $Z \otimes X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![(1.10)  backward ∘ forward = id](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** After level exchange the cup $\Omega$ and the cap $\omega$ form a zigzag, and **(2.1) right zigzag** removes it, leaving the box $\alpha$.

Steps, side by side: side 1: (2.1) right zigzag; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\alpha
$$

![(1.10)  backward ∘ forward = id, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### (1.10)  forward ∘ backward = id

The other composite of (1.10): starting from $\beta\colon T\otimes Y\to Z$ and going back and forth gives $\beta$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
ω : X ⊗ Y → 𝟙
Ω : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
Ω′ : 𝟙 → Y ⊗ X
pairing ω Ω
pairing ω Ω′
α : T → Z ⊗ X
β : T ⊗ Y → Z
```

```
(id_Z ⊗ ω)((β ⊗ id_X)(id_T ⊗ Ω) ⊗ id_Y) = β
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{id}_{Z} \otimes \omega) \\
&\;(((\beta \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X}) (\mathrm{id}_{T} \otimes \Omega)) \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y})
\end{aligned}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\beta
$$

a morphism from $T \otimes Y$ to $Z$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![(1.10)  forward ∘ backward = id](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** This time the **(2.1) left zigzag** does the work.

Steps, side by side: side 1: (2.1) left zigzag; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\beta
$$

![(1.10)  forward ∘ backward = id, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

## 6. §2.1.2 Left duals: ∨f and the identities (2.2)

### §2.1.2  definition of ∨f

§2.1.2: with left duals, $\mathrm{ev}_X\colon {}^{\vee}X\otimes X\to\mathbb 1$ is a cap and $\mathrm{coev}_X\colon\mathbb 1\to X\otimes{}^{\vee}X$ is a cup. The dual of $f\colon X\to Y$ is ${}^{\vee}f = (\mathrm{ev}_Y\otimes\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}X})(\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}Y}\otimes f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}X})(\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}Y}\otimes\mathrm{coev}_X)$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → Y
```

```
∨f = (ev_Y ⊗ id_∨X)(id_∨Y ⊗ f ⊗ id_∨X)(id_∨Y ⊗ coev_X)
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
{}^{\vee}f
$$

$$=$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{ev}_{Y} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}X}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}Y} \otimes f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}X}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}Y} \otimes \mathrm{coev}_{X})
\end{aligned}
$$

a morphism from ${}^{\vee}Y$ to ${}^{\vee}X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§2.1.2  definition of ∨f](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** With **duals: ∨X**, `ev_X`, `coev_X` and `∨f` are built in for every declared box. The rule **definition of ∨f** folds the three-layer picture into the single box ${}^{\vee}f$.

Steps, side by side: side 1: already in normal form; side 2: definition of ∨f.

Normal form:

$$
{}^{\vee}f
$$

![§2.1.2  definition of ∨f, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### (2.2) left: slide through ev

Formula (2.2), left: a dual box slides through a cap, $\mathrm{ev}_X({}^{\vee}f\otimes\mathrm{id}_X)=\mathrm{ev}_Y(\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}Y}\otimes f)$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → Y
```

```
ev_X(∨f ⊗ id_X) = ev_Y(id_∨Y ⊗ f)
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\mathrm{ev}_{X} ({}^{\vee}f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X}) \;=\; \mathrm{ev}_{Y} (\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}Y} \otimes f)
$$

a morphism from ${}^{\vee}Y \otimes X$ to $\mathbb{1}$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![(2.2) left: slide through ev](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The rule **(2.2) slide through ev** moves the box from the left leg of the cap to the right leg, turning ${}^{\vee}f$ into $f$.

Steps, side by side: side 1: (2.2) slide through ev; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{ev}_{Y} (\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}Y} \otimes f)
$$

![(2.2) left: slide through ev, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### (2.2) right: slide through coev

Formula (2.2), right: $(\mathrm{id}_Y\otimes{}^{\vee}f)\mathrm{coev}_Y=(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}X})\mathrm{coev}_X$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → Y
```

```
(id_Y ⊗ ∨f)coev_Y = (f ⊗ id_∨X)coev_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
(\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes {}^{\vee}f) \mathrm{coev}_{Y} \;=\; (f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}X}) \mathrm{coev}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $\mathbb{1}$ to $Y \otimes {}^{\vee}X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![(2.2) right: slide through coev](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The rule **(2.2) slide through coev** does the same through a cup.

Steps, side by side: side 1: (2.2) slide through coev; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
(f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{{}^{\vee}X}) \mathrm{coev}_{X}
$$

![(2.2) right: slide through coev, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### Zigzag for ev/coev

The duality identity $(\mathrm{id}_X\otimes\mathrm{ev}_X)(\mathrm{coev}_X\otimes\mathrm{id}_X)=\mathrm{id}_X$: ev and coev form a non-degenerate pairing.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → Y
```

```

### §2.6.2  isomorphic objects have the same dimension

§2.6.2: isomorphic objects have the same dimensions. For an isomorphism $u\colon X\to Y$ with inverse $u'$, $\dim_l(X) = \mathrm{tr}_l(u'u) = \mathrm{tr}_l(uu') = \dim_l(Y)$. The signature line `inverse u u′` declares $u'$ the inverse of $u$.

u′ : Y → X
inverse u u′

```

$$

$$=$$

$$

$$

a morphism from $\mathbb{1}$ to $\mathbb{1}$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§2.6.2  isomorphic objects have the same dimension](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** **trace symmetry** first turns the right side so that it starts at $u$, then **inverse boxes** cancels $u'u$ on both sides, leaving $\dim_l(X)$.

\mathrm{ev}_{X} \widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_{X}
$$

§2.7.1: a spherical category is a pivotal category whose left and right traces agree, $\mathrm{tr}_l(f) = \mathrm{tr}_r(f)$. This example switches on **spherical** under the buttons.

Lemma 2.9: in a spherical category, a closed diagram may be moved on the sphere $S^2$. Pushing a strand across the point at infinity turns a right trace into a left trace; here $\mathrm{tr}_r(qp)$ on $X$ becomes $\mathrm{tr}_l(pq)$ on $Y$.

$$

a morphism from $\mathbb{1}$ to $\mathbb{1}$.

### §2.7.3  Lemma 2.10: tr_l(j f p) = tr_l(f)

§2.7.3, Lemma 2.10: in the category of projective modules, the left trace is the Hattori–Stallings trace. A projective module $X$ sits in a free module $Y$ with inclusion $j$ and projection $p$, so $pj = \mathrm{id}_X$; the proof is $\mathrm{tr}_l(jfp) = \mathrm{tr}_l(fpj) = \mathrm{tr}_l(f)$. The signature line `retract p j` declares $pj = \mathrm{id}_X$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
j : X → Y
p : Y → X
retract p j
```

```
ev_Y(id_Y* ⊗ j f p)coev~_Y = ev_X(id_X* ⊗ f)coev~_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\mathrm{ev}_{Y} (\mathrm{id}_{Y^{*}} \otimes (j f p)) \widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_{Y}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\mathrm{ev}_{X} (\mathrm{id}_{X^{*}} \otimes f) \widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $\mathbb{1}$ to $\mathbb{1}$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§2.7.3  Lemma 2.10: tr_l(j f p) = tr_l(f)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** **trace symmetry** turns the loop so that it starts at $f$; then $j$ sits directly below $p$ and **retract (§2.7.3)** removes them. (Exercise 2.7.4, on equivalent pivotal categories, is a statement about functors and is not in the editor.)

Steps, side by side: side 1: trace symmetry (§2.6.1) → retract (§2.7.3); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{ev}_{X} (\mathrm{id}_{X^{*}} \otimes f) \widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_{X}
$$

## 13. §3.1 Braidings and symmetries

### (3.1)  τ_{X,Y⊗Z} = (id_Y ⊗ τ_{X,Z})(τ_{X,Y} ⊗ id_Z)

Chapter 3, §3.1.1: a braiding is a natural family of isomorphisms $\tau_{X,Y}\colon X\otimes Y\to Y\otimes X$, drawn as a crossing in which the strand from $X$ passes over (Figure 3.1). It is ⊗-multiplicative: (3.1) $\tau_{X,Y\otimes Z} = (\mathrm{id}_Y\otimes\tau_{X,Z})(\tau_{X,Y}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Z)$. Type it as `τ_{X,Y⊗Z}`.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
g : Y → Y
```

```
τ_{X,Y⊗Z} = (id_Y ⊗ τ_{X,Z})(τ_{X,Y} ⊗ id_Z)
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\tau_{X,Y \otimes Z} \;=\; (\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes \tau_{X,Z}) (\tau_{X,Y} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Z})
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes Y \otimes Z$ to $Y \otimes Z \otimes X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![(3.1)  τ_{X,Y⊗Z} = (id_Y ⊗ τ_{X,Z})(τ_{X,Y} ⊗ id_Z)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The rule **braiding on ⊗ (3.1)–(3.3)** splits the crossing of $X$ over the pair $Y\otimes Z$ into two crossings of single strands. With the unit, (3.3) $\tau_{X,\mathbb 1} = \tau_{\mathbb 1,X} = \mathrm{id}_X$, the same rule removes the box.

Steps, side by side: side 1: braiding on ⊗ (3.1)–(3.3); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
(\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes \tau_{X,Z}) (\tau_{X,Y} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Z})
$$

![(3.1)  τ_{X,Y⊗Z} = (id_Y ⊗ τ_{X,Z})(τ_{X,Y} ⊗ id_Z), simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### §3.1.1  naturality: τ_{X,Y}(f ⊗ g) = (g ⊗ f)τ_{X,Y}

Naturality of the braiding: $\tau_{X',Y'}(f\otimes g) = (g\otimes f)\tau_{X,Y}$ for $f\colon X\to X'$ and $g\colon Y\to Y'$. Boxes slide along the strands through the crossing.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

### Exercise 3.1.12  the Yang–Baxter equation

Exercise 3.1.12: every braiding satisfies the Yang–Baxter equation $(\tau_{Y,Z}\otimes\mathrm{id}_X)(\mathrm{id}_Y\otimes\tau_{X,Z})(\tau_{X,Y}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Z) = (\mathrm{id}_Z\otimes\tau_{X,Y})(\tau_{X,Z}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Y)(\mathrm{id}_X\otimes\tau_{Y,Z})$. Pictorially it is the Reidemeister move R3: a strand slides over a crossing.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
g : Y → Y
```

```
(τ_{Y,Z} ⊗ id_X)(id_Y ⊗ τ_{X,Z})(τ_{X,Y} ⊗ id_Z) = (id_Z ⊗ τ_{X,Y})(τ_{X,Z} ⊗ id_Y)(id_X ⊗ τ_{Y,Z})
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\tau_{Y,Z} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes \tau_{X,Z}) \\
&\;(\tau_{X,Y} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Z})
\end{aligned}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{id}_{Z} \otimes \tau_{X,Y}) \\
&\;(\tau_{X,Z} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \tau_{Y,Z})
\end{aligned}
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes Y \otimes Z$ to $Z \otimes Y \otimes X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![Exercise 3.1.12  the Yang–Baxter equation](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The rule **R3: Yang–Baxter** rewrites three consecutive crossings of the same kind, on positions $a, a+1, a$, into the order $a+1, a, a+1$.

Steps, side by side: side 1: R3: Yang–Baxter; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{id}_{Z} \otimes \tau_{X,Y}) \\
&\;(\tau_{X,Z} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \tau_{Y,Z})
\end{aligned}
$$

![Exercise 3.1.12  the Yang–Baxter equation, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

## 14. §3.2 The Reidemeister calculus

### R2  τ⁻¹_{X,Y} τ_{X,Y} = id

§3.2.2, the move R2: a crossing followed by the inverse crossing on the same two strands is the identity.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
g : Y → Y
```

```
τ⁻¹_{X,Y} τ_{X,Y} = id_X ⊗ id_Y
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\tau^{-1}_{X,Y} \tau_{X,Y} \;=\; \mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y}
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes Y$ to $X \otimes Y$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![R2  τ⁻¹_{X,Y} τ_{X,Y} = id](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** **R2 (§3.2.2)** removes the pair.

Steps, side by side: side 1: R2 (§3.2.2); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{id}_{X \otimes Y}
$$

![R2  τ⁻¹_{X,Y} τ_{X,Y} = id, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### R3  with inverse crossings

R3 for crossings of the other kind: the Yang–Baxter equation also holds for the inverse crossings $\tau^{-1}$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
g : Y → Y
```

```
(τ⁻¹_{Z,Y} ⊗ id_X)(id_Y ⊗ τ⁻¹_{Z,X})(τ⁻¹_{Y,X} ⊗ id_Z) = (id_Z ⊗ τ⁻¹_{Y,X})(τ⁻¹_{Z,X} ⊗ id_Y)(id_X ⊗ τ⁻¹_{Z,Y})
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\tau^{-1}_{Z,Y} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes \tau^{-1}_{Z,X}) \\
&\;(\tau^{-1}_{Y,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Z})
\end{aligned}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{id}_{Z} \otimes \tau^{-1}_{Y,X}) \\
&\;(\tau^{-1}_{Z,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \tau^{-1}_{Z,Y})
\end{aligned}
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes Y \otimes Z$ to $Z \otimes Y \otimes X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![R3  with inverse crossings](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** **R3: Yang–Baxter** applies to three crossings of the same kind, positive or negative.

Steps, side by side: side 1: R3: Yang–Baxter; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{id}_{Z} \otimes \tau^{-1}_{Y,X}) \\
&\;(\tau^{-1}_{Z,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \tau^{-1}_{Z,Y})
\end{aligned}
$$

![R3  with inverse crossings, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### R4  a strand passes over a box

R4: a strand that passes over a box can be pushed off it. In formulas this is the naturality of $\tau_{X,Y}$ in $X$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
g : Y → Y
```

```
(id_Y ⊗ f)τ_{X,Y} = τ_{X,Y}(f ⊗ id_Y)
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
(\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes f) \tau_{X,Y} \;=\; \tau_{X,Y} (f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y})
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes Y$ to $Y \otimes X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![R4  a strand passes over a box](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** **R4, R5: naturality of τ** moves the box below the crossing.

Steps, side by side: side 1: R4, R5: naturality of τ; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\tau_{X,Y} (f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y})
$$

![R4  a strand passes over a box, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### R5  a strand passes under a box

R5: the same for a strand that passes under a box, the naturality of the inverse crossing.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
g : Y → Y
```

```
(id_Y ⊗ f)τ⁻¹_{Y,X} = τ⁻¹_{Y,X}(f ⊗ id_Y)
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
(\mathrm{id}_{Y} \otimes f) \tau^{-1}_{Y,X} \;=\; \tau^{-1}_{Y,X} (f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y})
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes Y$ to $Y \otimes X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![R5  a strand passes under a box](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The same rule moves the box through $\tau^{-1}_{Y,X}$.

Steps, side by side: side 1: R4, R5: naturality of τ; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\tau^{-1}_{Y,X} (f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y})
$$

![R5  a strand passes under a box, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### Lemma 3.1  an upward strand crosses a box

Lemma 3.1 says that the Reidemeister moves R2–R5 preserve the morphism of a Reidemeister diagram, also when strands point up. Here the crossing is on an upward strand coloured $X^*$, with duals written $X^*$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
g : Y → Y
```

```
(g ⊗ id_X*)τ_{X*,Y} = τ_{X*,Y}(id_X* ⊗ g)
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
(g \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X^{*}}) \tau_{X^{*},Y} \;=\; \tau_{X^{*},Y} (\mathrm{id}_{X^{*}} \otimes g)
$$

a morphism from $X^{*} \otimes Y$ to $Y \otimes X^{*}$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![Lemma 3.1  an upward strand crosses a box](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The box slides through the crossing just as before: in the layered form an upward strand is simply a strand coloured $X^*$. (The move R1 needs the twists of §3.3; see Theorem 3.3 below.)

Steps, side by side: side 1: R4, R5: naturality of τ; side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\tau_{X^{*},Y} (\mathrm{id}_{X^{*}} \otimes g)
$$

![Lemma 3.1  an upward strand crosses a box, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

## 15. §3.1.2 Symmetries and Remark 3.2.3

### §3.1.2  a symmetry: τ_{Y,X} τ_{X,Y} = id

§3.1.2: a braiding is symmetric when $\tau_{Y,X}\tau_{X,Y} = \mathrm{id}_{X\otimes Y}$, as for the flip of sets or vector spaces (Examples 3.1.3–3.1.4) and the signed flip of super vector spaces (Example 3.1.5). This example switches on **symmetric** under the buttons.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
g : Y → Y
```

```
τ_{Y,X} τ_{X,Y} = id_X ⊗ id_Y
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\tau_{Y,X} \tau_{X,Y} \;=\; \mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y}
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes Y$ to $X \otimes Y$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§3.1.2  a symmetry: τ_{Y,X} τ_{X,Y} = id](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** With **symmetric** on, the rule **τ_Y,X τ_X,Y = id (§3.1.2)** removes two crossings of the same kind stacked on the same strands. Without it the equation is (rightly) not proved.

Steps, side by side: side 1: τ_Y,X τ_X,Y = id (§3.1.2); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{id}_{X \otimes Y}
$$

![§3.1.2  a symmetry: τ_{Y,X} τ_{X,Y} = id, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### Remark 3.2.3  over- and under-passes agree

Remark 3.2.3: for a symmetric braiding the two crossings of Figure 3.1 are the same morphism, $\tau^{-1}_{Y,X} = \tau_{X,Y}$, so over- and under-passes do not matter.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
f : X → X
g : Y → Y
```

```
τ⁻¹_{Y,X} = τ_{X,Y}
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\tau^{-1}_{Y,X} \;=\; \tau_{X,Y}
$$

a morphism from $X \otimes Y$ to $Y \otimes X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![Remark 3.2.3  over- and under-passes agree](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** **symmetry (§3.1.2)** turns every under-crossing into the over-crossing.

Steps, side by side: side 1: symmetry (§3.1.2); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\tau_{X,Y}
$$

![Remark 3.2.3  over- and under-passes agree, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

## 16. §3.3.1 Twists and Lemma 3.2

### §3.3.1  the left twist θˡ_X is a curl

§3.3.1: in a braided pivotal category the **left twist** is the curl $\theta^l_X = (\mathrm{ev}_X \otimes \mathrm{id}_X)(\mathrm{id}_{X^*} \otimes \tau_{X,X})(\widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_X \otimes \mathrm{id}_X)$: the strand makes a loop to the left and crosses over itself. The twists are built in, typed `θˡ_X`, `θʳ_X`, `θˡ⁻¹_X` and `θʳ⁻¹_X` (keypad *Greek* for θ; ˡ and ʳ are the modifier letters).

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
g : X → Y
k : X → X
```

```
(ev_X ⊗ id_X)(id_X* ⊗ τ_{X,X})(coev~_X ⊗ id_X) = θˡ_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{ev}_{X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X^{*}} \otimes \tau_{X,X}) \\
&\;(\widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_{X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X})
\end{aligned}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\mathrm{\theta ^{l}}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§3.3.1  the left twist θˡ_X is a curl](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** **twist fold (§3.3.1)** recognises the cup $\widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_X$, the crossing and the cap $\mathrm{ev}_X$ and replaces the three by one box $\theta^l_X$.

Steps, side by side: side 1: twist fold (§3.3.1); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{\theta ^{l}}_{X}
$$

![§3.3.1  the left twist θˡ_X is a curl, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### §3.3.1  the right twist θʳ_X is a curl

§3.3.1: the **right twist** $\theta^r_X = (\mathrm{id}_X \otimes \widetilde{\mathrm{ev}}_X)(\tau_{X,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X^*})(\mathrm{id}_X \otimes \mathrm{coev}_X)$ is the mirror curl, a loop to the right.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
g : X → Y
k : X → X
```

```
(id_X ⊗ ev~_X)(τ_{X,X} ⊗ id_X*)(id_X ⊗ coev_X) = θʳ_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \widetilde{\mathrm{ev}}_{X}) \\
&\;(\tau_{X,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X^{*}}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \mathrm{coev}_{X})
\end{aligned}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\mathrm{\theta ^{r}}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§3.3.1  the right twist θʳ_X is a curl](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The same rule folds the right-hand curl into $\theta^r_X$.

Steps, side by side: side 1: twist fold (§3.3.1); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{\theta ^{r}}_{X}
$$

![§3.3.1  the right twist θʳ_X is a curl, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### Lemma 3.2  (θˡ_X)⁻¹ is the curl with τ⁻¹

Lemma 3.2: the twists are invertible, and the inverse of $\theta^l_X$ is the right-hand curl with the inverse crossing, $(\theta^l_X)^{-1} = (\mathrm{id}_X \otimes \widetilde{\mathrm{ev}}_X)(\tau^{-1}_{X,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X^*})(\mathrm{id}_X \otimes \mathrm{coev}_X)$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
g : X → Y
k : X → X
```

```
(id_X ⊗ ev~_X)(τ⁻¹_{X,X} ⊗ id_X*)(id_X ⊗ coev_X) = θˡ⁻¹_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \widetilde{\mathrm{ev}}_{X}) \\
&\;(\tau^{-1}_{X,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X^{*}}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \mathrm{coev}_{X})
\end{aligned}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\mathrm{\theta ^{l}}^{-1}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

**Simplify.** **twist fold (§3.3.1)** reads the sign of the crossing: a right-hand curl with $\tau^{-1}$ becomes $\theta^{l\,-1}_X$.

Steps, side by side: side 1: twist fold (§3.3.1); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{\theta ^{l}}^{-1}_{X}
$$

![Lemma 3.2  (θˡ_X)⁻¹ is the curl with τ⁻¹, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### Lemma 3.2  θˡ_X (θˡ_X)⁻¹ = id, the curls drawn out

Lemma 3.2 drawn out: $\theta^l_X(\theta^l_X)^{-1} = \mathrm{id}_X$ with both curls written as cups, crossings and caps.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
g : X → Y
k : X → X
```

```
(ev_X ⊗ id_X)(id_X* ⊗ τ_{X,X})(coev~_X ⊗ id_X)(id_X ⊗ ev~_X)(τ⁻¹_{X,X} ⊗ id_X*)(id_X ⊗ coev_X) = id_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

&\;(\tau^{-1}_{X,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X^{*}}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \mathrm{coev}_{X})
\end{aligned}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\mathrm{id}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![Lemma 3.2  θˡ_X (θˡ_X)⁻¹ = id, the curls drawn out](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** In the normal form the layers of the two curls interleave, so the fold follows each curl's strands past layers that do not touch them (level exchange). It folds the curl with $\tau^{-1}$ first, then the other, and **twists cancel (Lemma 3.2)** removes $\theta^l_X$ with its inverse.

Steps, side by side: side 1: twist fold (§3.3.1) → twist fold (§3.3.1) → twists cancel (Lemma 3.2); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{id}_{X}
$$

![Lemma 3.2  θˡ_X (θˡ_X)⁻¹ = id, the curls drawn out, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

## 18. §3.3.2 Ribbon categories

### §3.3.2  ribbon: θˡ_X = θʳ_X

§3.3.2: a braided pivotal category is **ribbon** when $\theta^l_X = \theta^r_X$ for all $X$; the common value is the twist $\theta_X$. This example switches on **ribbon** under the buttons.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
g : X → Y
k : X → X
```

```
θˡ_X = θʳ_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\mathrm{\theta ^{l}}_{X} \;=\; \mathrm{\theta ^{r}}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![§3.3.2  ribbon: θˡ_X = θʳ_X](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** With **ribbon** on, **ribbon: θʳ = θˡ (§3.3.2)** writes every right twist as the left twist. Without it the equation is (rightly) not proved: in a braided pivotal category the two twists can differ.

Steps, side by side: side 1: already in normal form; side 2: ribbon: θʳ = θˡ (§3.3.2).

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{\theta ^{l}}_{X}
$$

![§3.3.2  ribbon: θˡ_X = θʳ_X, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### Theorem 3.3  R1: θʳ_X (θˡ_X)⁻¹ = id

Theorem 3.3: in a ribbon category the move R1 holds: a right-hand curl followed by a left-hand curl with the inverse crossing is the identity, since it is $\theta^r_X(\theta^l_X)^{-1} = \mathrm{id}_X$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
g : X → Y
k : X → X
```

```
(id_X ⊗ ev~_X)(τ_{X,X} ⊗ id_X*)(id_X ⊗ coev_X)(id_X ⊗ ev~_X)(τ⁻¹_{X,X} ⊗ id_X*)(id_X ⊗ coev_X) = id_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \widetilde{\mathrm{ev}}_{X}) \\
&\;(\tau_{X,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X^{*}}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \mathrm{coev}_{X}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \widetilde{\mathrm{ev}}_{X}) \\
&\;(\tau^{-1}_{X,X} \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X^{*}}) \\
&\;(\mathrm{id}_{X} \otimes \mathrm{coev}_{X})
\end{aligned}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\mathrm{id}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $X$ to $X$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![Theorem 3.3  R1: θʳ_X (θˡ_X)⁻¹ = id](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** The two curls fold to $\theta^r_X$ and $\theta^{l\,-1}_X$, **ribbon** makes the first $\theta^l_X$, and **twists cancel** finishes.

Steps, side by side: side 1: twist fold (§3.3.1) → twist fold (§3.3.1) → ribbon: θʳ = θˡ (§3.3.2) → twists cancel (Lemma 3.2); side 2: already in normal form.

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{id}_{X}
$$

![Theorem 3.3  R1: θʳ_X (θˡ_X)⁻¹ = id, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

### Corollary 3.4  a ribbon category is spherical

Corollary 3.4: a ribbon category is spherical, $\mathrm{tr}_l(k) = \mathrm{tr}_r(k)$.

**Type it.** Signature and expression:

```
g : X → Y
k : X → X
```

```
ev_X(id_X* ⊗ k)coev~_X = ev~_X(k ⊗ id_X*)coev_X
```

**Symbolic.** The editor typesets it as

$$
\mathrm{ev}_{X} (\mathrm{id}_{X^{*}} \otimes k) \widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_{X}
$$

$$=$$

$$
\widetilde{\mathrm{ev}}_{X} (k \otimes \mathrm{id}_{X^{*}}) \mathrm{coev}_{X}
$$

a morphism from $\mathbb{1}$ to $\mathbb{1}$.

**Graphical.** Expression → Diagram draws:

![Corollary 3.4  a ribbon category is spherical](data:image/png;base64,)

**Simplify.** With **ribbon** on, the editor (like the kernel) also uses **sphericity (§2.7.1)**, which turns the right loop into the left loop.

Steps, side by side: side 1: already in normal form; side 2: sphericity (§2.7.1).

Normal form:

$$
\mathrm{ev}_{X} (\mathrm{id}_{X^{*}} \otimes k) \widetilde{\mathrm{coev}}_{X}
$$

![Corollary 3.4  a ribbon category is spherical, simplified](data:image/png;base64,)

The editor reports: *✓ Both sides reduce to the same normal form, so the equation holds.*

## 19. The two engines

Simplify can run on either of two engines, chosen with **engine** under the buttons:

- **JavaScript (offline):** a port of the Wolfram notebook engine, with the same layered form, the same level exchange and the same rules in the same order. It needs no network.
- **Wolfram kernel:** the page sends the layered form to the `GraphicalCalculusKernel` API in the Wolfram Cloud, which runs the rules of the Wolfram notebooks (`graphical-calculus-2.1-simplify.nb`, `pivotal-2.1.3.wl`, `penrose-2.2.wl`, `pivotal-2.3-2.7.wl`, `braided-2.7-3.2.wl`, `ribbon-3.3.wl`). The page then compares the kernel's answer with the JavaScript engine and reports any difference.

For §2.3–2.7 the editor works in a strict pivotal category: it identifies $X^{**}$ with $X$ and $\psi_X$ with $\mathrm{id}_X$. The Wolfram notebook `graphical-calculus-2.3-2.7.nb` keeps $X^{**}$ apart from $X$, draws $\psi_X$ as a box, and proves Lemmas 2.2–2.4, Exercise 2.3.3 and Theorem 2.7 (strand by strand) with it; for the editor's inputs the kernel uses the strict forms of the same rules.

For §3.3 the notebook `graphical-calculus-3.3.nb` also checks, in graded vector spaces with weights, that the model with weight 2 is braided pivotal but not ribbon, that the weights ±1 give a ribbon category, the duals of twists in Lemma 3.2, (3.4), Corollary 3.4, Lemma 3.5 for super vector spaces and Lemma 3.6.

On every example in this document, both engines give the same sequence of rules and the same result. In the Wolfram notebooks the same identities are also checked in vector spaces, where $\otimes$ is the Kronecker product and composition is the matrix product.
